title: Yi XIANG

Presentations:

2027: Beijing Normal University (Zhuhai); SUFE
2026: The 18th International Symposium on Human Capital and Labor Markets (CUFE, Beijing); Asian and Australasian Society of Labour Economics Conference (PKU, Beijing); ES Australasia Meeting (Adelaide University, Australia); Asian SPACE Workshop (SJTU-HKUST, HK); Jobs and Development Conference (HKUST, HK); CES Annual Meeting (SUFE, Chengdu); ES North American Summer Meeting (Emory University,US); Xi’an Jiaotong University; RCEA International Conference on Economics, Econometrics, and Finance (Universidad Pontificia de Comillas, Spain); PhD Brownbag (HKU)
2022-2025: PhD Brownbag (×2, HKU); Graduate Seminar (HKU)



Abstract

Farmers may damper from the labor shortage in agricultural production, incentivizing them to transform modernization. This paper documents that population aging increases dramatically over time, especially in the rural areas, whereas the responses of the agricultural mechanization, at the micro level, remain relatively stable in the early stage and start to decrease dramatically, which is inconsistent with the remorseless increase in aggregate. A model is proposed to reconcile this puzzling fact, where heterogeneous labor decides where to work and whether to adopt machinery simultaneously. I show that the more population aging, the agricultural labor productivity reacts nonlinearly and shows an initial plateau and subsequent negative trend turning at age 40, which is partly driven by the nonlinear agricultural mechanization. Further, the rapid development of non-agriculture and the decrease of the overall migration cost due to, for example, the hukou reform, attract more labor sort to the non-agricultural sector, and a higher agricultural mechanization can be accommodated in equilibrium because the selection effect exceeds the labor-mobility barrier effect.




Presentations:

2026: 1st Altitude Conference on Growth and Development (Xizang University, Lsaha); CES Presidential Forum 2026 (UIBE, Beijing); Huazhong University of Science and Technology (HUST, Wuhan)

title: Yi XIANG
text:
Welcome! I am Yi XIANG (向意)
I am an Econ Ph.D. candidate in the Business School at the University of Hong Kong (HKU). I received my master’s degree from the Chinese University of Hong Kong and my bachelor’s degree from Sichuan University. I will be on the job market in 2026-2027.
You can reach me at: xiangyi@connect.hku.hk
